summary: A declarative language for governance constraints on the actions of AI systems and AI agents. A program is a policy graph evaluated before any action is released, on a tamper-evident log.
well_formedness: every cord is a permitted endpoint pairing
every gate lies on a path to the master

every delegation satisfies the no-amplification invariant (risk subset and, pairwise, grade(delegate) not above grade(delegator) in the active-ladder order; additionally an ungraded delegator caps the delegate at ungraded)
a gate declaring a required grade is a source gate; grade_required on a non-source (piped) gate is ill-formed at apply
evaluation: One transport evaluates the whole graph; every activated gate gets a verdict; effective verdicts propagate strictest-wins along pipes; the master releases a terminal gate's action iff its effective verdict is auto and every egress obligation is attached.
litmus: A regulation names it as a declaration -> language. A deployment chooses its values -> policy. A runtime does it -> host. A guard ranges only over declared token properties, never a computed value, and never over grade (a config attribute: granted on actor, required on a source gate). The autonomy ladder and its order are policy (vocabulary/grades.json, default L0..L4, remappable); the language requires an active total order and owns only the §7.1 comparison/gating rule evaluated at the source gate.
